title: Beating hull speed
brief: Worked example. Scrub the timeline to watch the reasoning fixate, then break. Events 3–6 are what naval architecture actually did for a century; event 7 is the piece of knowledge that made an expansive partition thinkable.

node.text: Hull speed ≈ 1.34 × √(waterline length in ft) knots. Past it, the hull is climbing its own bow wave.

events.summary: Seeded the constraint everyone treats as a law of nature.

node.text: Wave-making resistance rises roughly with the sixth power of speed near hull speed.

node.proposition: There exists a vessel that travels far faster than the hull speed of its waterline length.
node.note: Undecidable against K0–K1: they say the cost is prohibitive, not that it is impossible.

node.proposition: There exists a vessel that beats hull speed by installing more engine.
There exists a vessel that beats a given hull speed by being longer.
node.note: Works, but it moves the constraint instead of removing it.

events.summary: Second partition — also restrictive. The tree is fixating.

events.note: K1 settles this directly — a restrictive partition K can decide was never a concept.

events.summary: C2 set aside — the archetypal fixated answer.

node.text: Wave-making resistance is a consequence of displacing water at the surface. It is not a property of 'boats' as such.
node.source: K→K on K0/K1 — is the constraint a law, or an artefact of the usual implementation?

events.summary: The unlock: the constraint belongs to displacement, not to boats.

node.breaks: the definition of a boat as a body supported by buoyancy
node.proposition: There exists a vessel that moves over water without displacing it.

events.summary: K2 supplied the attribute that broke buoyancy.

node.text: A submerged foil generates lift proportional to v². Above a threshold speed, lift can exceed vessel weight.

node.proposition: There exists a vessel lifted clear of the surface by foils while remaining in the water.
node.note: Restrictive *relative to C3* — once you accept a non-displacing vessel, foils are a known means.

node.proposition: There exists a vessel that rides on a cushion of pressurised air.

node.breaks: the assumption that the cargo travels inside a single rigid vessel
node.proposition: There exists a way to move cargo over water with no vessel at all.
node.note: Still open. K is empty here — that is the signal to run K→K.

events.summary: Partitioned C3 — a second expansive step.

node.text: A hydrofoil craft exists and sustains 40+ knots: the hull leaves the water, so displacement drag goes to zero.
node.source: conjunction of C4 — Forlanini 1906, Supramar PT10 1952

node.text: An air-cushion vehicle carries commercial loads over water and land alike; the cushion, not the hull, bears the weight.

events.summary: C5 closed. Two conjunctions from one expansive partition.

node.text: Whether a self-guiding cargo unit can navigate open water unaided at commercial scale.

events.summary: C6 remains open; this is the lead that would decide it.
